creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`./dev` died in CI at `os = os_raw.trim()` - "Value '0' (int) is not
compatible with expected type 'str'" - while passing on every
contributor's machine. Both were running "rad v0.11.0".

Rad fills a shell capture by name when every target is spelled `stdout`,
`stderr` or `code`, and by position otherwise. Rad v0.12 reorders the
positional form from (code, stdout, stderr) to (stdout, stderr, code).
`./dev` was written against a local build past the v0.11.0 tag, where
`os_raw = $\`uname -s\`` yields "Darwin"; under the released v0.11.0 that
`deps/rad.pin` names and CI installs, the same line yields the exit code.

Six captures used names of their own and were rewritten to the named
form, which means the same thing under both Rads. One of them,
`_, stderr, code = $\`curl ...\``, was silently binding curl's stderr to
`code` under the pinned Rad - it had not been reached yet, and would have
surfaced as a download failure reported with the wrong text. The rule is
now written down at the top of `./dev` rather than left to be
rediscovered.

Verified by running the whole gate under the pinned v0.11.0 binary,
fetched and checksummed the way the workflow fetches it, as well as under
the local build.

Worth noticing: the pin's own comment says it "names the Rad the gate is
written against", and for a while it did not. Nothing checks that claim,
and nothing can from inside a script that is already running under the
answer. Living with it - the gate is the check, now that the gate can
actually run - but if it recurs, the cheap version is CI printing the
pinned version beside `rad --version` and failing on a mismatch.
title: 🛠️ The gate ran on a Rad the script was not written against
